- **THM-4750 / HYP-9361 (AUDITED 2026-10-21, mac-mini-2026-10-21-fanopsp; MISTAKE-654; [THM-4750](../../01-canon/theorems/THM-4750-the-camion-function-half-speed-interpolation-and-the-camion-lift.md), [audit](../results/camion_function_audit_20261021.md)):** the Camion function. Strong tournament counts interpolate p-adically along classes mod p-1 at HALF the Kummer speed (v_p Delta^i >= ceil(i/2), from the Session25 filtered algebra; speed 1/r for r-uniform hypergraphs). Mod p^2 every class is a quadratic in l with curvature -q_2(p) X(m-2), where X counts tournaments made strong by one two-way pair. So the Wieferich primes 1093, 3511 run at full speed, with exactly 1 second-order root per Camion zero class (0 or 2 elsewhere, 1:1 over 1226 primes; a double root can be RAMIFIED, M1); base 3 (semicomplete digraphs) runs at full speed exactly at p = 11. The Camion limit is Lambda_p = sigma_p - <2>^(-1/2), with sigma_p depending only on 2 mod p, and h(p) = v_p(2 - kappa(2)) for the Camion lift kappa(2) = omega(2) sigma_p^(-2), the unique base making every p^k a Camion pseudoprime (§5b, confirmed by a second audit pass, MISTAKE-655: tower height = v_p(a - kappa(a)) for all 794 bases tested). Camion-Wieferich primes <= 1e6: exactly 3, 13, 22409 (NEW; h = 2; FLINT search). p = 2 (Moon): the number of strong tournaments up to isomorphism is odd iff n is not 2 mod 3 (T = Phi_3 mod 2); the groupoid count has a 2-adic zero n*. HYP-9361: split/inert equidistribution, the S_r root law (r = 2, 3, 4 data), tower heights, and the irrationality of n*.

[HYP-9358](HYP-9358-camion-pseudoprimes-open-laws-wieferich-type-primes-sporadic-zero-classes-prime-squares.md) Camion-Wieferich infinitude, Poisson sporadic classes, counting, mod p^k for k >= 3, thresholds. title: "Camion pseudoprimes. Let s(m) be the number of strong labelled tournaments on m vertices (equivalently Hamiltonian by Camion's theorem for m >= 3; s(1) = 1 uses the strong-singleton convention) (A054946) and c(m) the number of circulant tournaments on Z_m (2^((m-1)/2) for odd m, 0 for even m >= 2). (1) For every odd prime p and every m >= 1, s(m+p-1) = (2/p) s(m) (mod p), and the same holds for D = s - c. (2) Hence s(kp) = (2/p)^k s(k) (mod p) and s(p) = (2/p) (mod p): the strong count obeys Euler's criterion. (3) Modulo 3 the strong exponential generating function is sin x; for odd n the moduli 3 and 5 impose no condition. (4) Korselt-type criterion: if n is composite with squarefree odd part, then s(n) = c(n) (mod n) iff p divides D(r_p) for every odd prime p | n, where r_p = n (mod p-1) taken in 1..p-1. (5) D(1) = D(2) = D(3) = 0 (K1, no strong K2, the triangle), so every Carmichael number, every 2p and every 3p is a Camion pseudoprime, and so is every 3ab with b >= 5 and a = 3b-2 both prime (both large primes in the triangle class 3, the factor 3 in class 1), in particular 4^q - 1 whenever the Mersenne number 2^q - 1 and the Wagstaff number (2^q+1)/3 are both prime; 21 = 3*7 is one and the base-2 pseudoprime 341 = 11*31 is not (its residue at 31 is the Wagstaff factor 11, and 31 does not divide D(11)), while 3*341 = 1023 = 2^10 - 1 is. (6) For odd n the tournament-count test 2^C(n,2) = c(n) (mod n) is the Fermat test to the base c(n) = 2^((n-1)/2); the universal residue sets of the two tests differ exactly by the triangle class 3. (7) Modulo p^2 (Lemma B of the independent audit): s(m + p(p-1)) = (2/p) s(m) (mod p^2) for all m >= 3; hence p^2 is a Camion pseudoprime iff p^2 | D(p) (only p = 3, 13 below 10000), the factor 9 never obstructs, and the criterion extends to cube-free odd parts. (8) The same quasi-periodicity holds for strong semicomplete digraphs (with (3/p), p >= 5) and, for m >= 2, for connected labelled graphs (Mani-Stones 2016; audit Lemma C): it is a property of the exponential family generated by 2^C(m,2) modulo p, not of the linear condensation. (9) Prime-power towers (with the Session25 prime-power law): D(p^a) = (2/p) D(p^(a-1)) (mod p^a), so the exponents a with p^a a Camion pseudoprime form an initial segment {1, ..., h(p)}, and h(p) equals the eventual (frozen) value of v_p(D(p^a)); for every odd prime p <= 10^4 the odd prime powers that are Camion pseudoprimes are exactly the primes, 9 and 169, mirroring the Wieferich bound for base-2 Fermat pseudoprimes."
